source.title: Euclidean random matrices: solved and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the Euclidean random-matrix setting attached to stationary points of a Hamiltonian H[x], where one studies the matrix M[x] at z = 0 and the measure built from exp(-βH[x]) together with determinant-based weights, can one construct a practical analytical formalism in which the BRST-type supersymmetry of the problem is not merely present formally but is used as a central working tool for computing the properties of the model?
accepted.context_brief: Practical supersymmetric formalism for Euclidean random matrices

evidence.quote: In the framework of Euclidean random theory there are two questions that are quite relevant and may be the most interesting for Euclidean Random theory: • How to construct and to use in a practical way a formalism where the supersymmetry of the problem plays a crucial role?

accepted.question_text: Within the same Euclidean random-matrix framework, does there exist a phase in which the BRST-type supersymmetry is spontaneously broken, and if such a phase exists, what physical effects follow from that supersymmetry breaking for the spectrum and related observables of the system?
accepted.context_brief: Spontaneous supersymmetry breaking and its physical effects

evidence.quote: • How to find out if there is a phase where supersymmetry is spontaneously broken and which are the physical effects of such a breaking.
